title: fix(app-shell): the sidebar Design entry opens the Studio surface the app bar Edit app opens (objectui#12520)
body:
Fixes #12520
Clause-②: no — a destination change inside the console shell, with no type, prop or export change.

## What changes

The console sidebar's ⋯ menu **Design** entry, and a favorite's Design entry, now open the same place the app bar's **Edit app** (pencil) opens for that item: its Studio surface. Before, they opened the metadata-admin page, which tells an admin that a packaged object is locked and cannot be edited.

- **One derivation for both controls.** `sidebarItemDesignPath` and `favoriteDesignPath` (in `SidebarItemMenu.tsx`) now call `appStudioRoutePath`, the function `AppHeader` uses for its pencil. They pass it the route the entry opens, in the same `{ type, name }` shape `AppHeader` reads from the URL. There is no second table.
  - `object` entry: `/studio/PACKAGE/data?surface=object:NAME`
  - `dashboard` entry: `/studio/PACKAGE/interfaces?surface=dashboard:NAME`
  - `page` entry: `/studio/PACKAGE/interfaces?surface=page:NAME`, which is what the app bar opens on a page today.
- **Which app.** A navigation entry uses the app whose navigation the sidebar draws (`activeApp`, which the sidebar already has). A favorite uses the app its own stored `href` names (`/apps/APP/...`), matched in the same `useMetadata().apps` the app bar reads. So a favorite starred in another app opens that app's package. No new read is added.
- **No Studio surface, no entry.** When the app has no owning package Studio can open (a runtime app, or the `sys_metadata` pseudo-package), `appStudioRoutePath` returns `null`. The Design entry then hides, as the app bar's pencil does. Nothing falls back to the metadata-admin route.
- **Unchanged.**
  - The gate: `isAdmin && canAuthorMetadata`, still read inside `SidebarItemMenu`.
  - Which entry types offer Design: `object`, `dashboard` and `page`; never `url`, `component`, records or apps.
  - `SidebarItemMenuProps`.
  - The metadata-admin route and page, `AppHeader.tsx`, and `appRoute.ts`.
  - The package entry: `appStudioRoutePath` is imported internally from `../utils/appRoute.js`, and no export is added.
- **Docs.** The `@object-ui/app-shell` README's "App → Studio reverse bridge" section now describes the sidebar's Design entry. The same edit corrects that section's object-route sentence: an object route opens `data?surface=object:NAME`, not the bare Data tab.
- Changeset: `.changeset/12520-design-entry-studio.md`, `@object-ui/app-shell` `patch`.

## Browser reading for the landing seat

At 1440 px on HotCRM, as an admin who may author metadata:

- Sidebar **Leads** ⋯ → **Design** should open the Studio Data surface for `crm_lead`: `/studio/app.objectstack.hotcrm/data?surface=object:crm_lead`.
- The app bar's pencil on the Leads list should open that same Studio Data surface for `crm_lead`.
- No "locked" notice on either path.

I did not take this reading. Per the dispatch, it belongs to the landing seat.

## Dispatch assumptions, measured on `c3de0bc73d`

- **A1 holds.** Both functions built `BASEPATH/metadata/TYPE/NAME`. Their only callers are `UnifiedSidebar` (`renderNavItemAction` and the content-favorite rows) and the 12427 test. `ObjectView`'s ⋯ menu is not a caller: it imports only `FavoriteMenuItem` and `useObjectListFavorite`.
- **A2 holds.** The sidebar already holds `activeApp` from the same `useMetadata().apps` catalog `AppHeader` reads. Favorites are global, not per app, so a favorite's app comes from its own `href`.
- **A3 holds and is pinned.** No owning package, or `sys_metadata`, gives `null`: the entry hides, and the app bar draws no pencil on that route either. For the three entry types the gate gives Design, `appStudioRoutePath` has a mapping, so the only `null` cases are the package cases.
- **A4 holds.** `src/index.ts` does not re-export `appStudioRoutePath`, and nothing is added.

## Tests

All runs are from the repo root, through the shared verify lock.

**New: `SidebarItemMenu.designOpensStudio-12520.test.tsx`.** It renders the real `AppHeader` on the route each entry opens, reads the Edit app button's href, and asserts that the entry's Design path is the same string. It covers:
- `object`, `dashboard` and `page` navigation entries;
- the matching favorites;
- a favorite starred in another app (it lands in that app's package);
- record, report and app favorites (`null`);
- the A3 cases: no package, `sys_metadata`, and a favorite whose `href` names no catalog app. In each, both sides answer `null`.

**Updated: `SidebarItemMenu-12427.test.tsx`.** The harness passes the app, and Design now lands on `/studio/com.acme.crm/data?surface=object:crm_lead`. The path tests now expect Studio paths. The gate tests (admin, authoring, and no entry for `url` / `component` / `separator` / `action`) are unchanged.

**Updated: `UnifiedSidebar.favoritesMenu-12427.test.tsx`.** Under A3, Design now hides for an app with no package, so the fixture app gets an owning package. Two click-through pins are added: the Leads entry, and a favorite from a second app. The gate assertions are unchanged.

**Final head `3c13a36aed`:**
- the affected union, 67 files: every `SidebarItemMenu*`, `UnifiedSidebar*`, `appRoute*` and `AppHeader*` test, the `ObjectView*` tests that name the ⋯ menu or favorites, every other test that renders `UnifiedSidebar` or `SidebarItemMenu`, and the three tests that read the app-shell README. Result: `Test Files 67 passed (67)`, `Tests 634 passed (634)`.
- the census and ratchet tests whose subject the diff touches, 85 files: every census or ratchet test under `packages/app-shell`, the cross-package censuses that read app-shell, and the `scripts/` tests over the test-file population. Result: `Test Files 85 passed (85)`, `Tests 2121 passed | 1 skipped (2122)`.

**Type-check.** `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exits 0 at `0353d94924`, after the dependency closure was built. The later commit changes only the README.

**Ablation.** I ran two legs, each through `ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode. The tool confirmed each mutation landed on disk and that the restore matched HEAD's blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`.
- **Leg 1:** `sidebarItemDesignPath` returns `/apps/APP/metadata/TYPE/NAME` again. 9 red, 27 green: the three navigation-entry parity pins, both A3 navigation pins, the 12427 Design-destination and path pins, and the sidebar's Leads click-through. The favorite pins and every gate test stayed green.
- **Leg 2:** `favoriteDesignPath` does the same. 4 red, 32 green: the favorite parity pin, the cross-app favorite (pure and click-through), and the no-package favorite case. I had predicted that last test would stay green, but its third assertion is an app without a package, so it went red.

## Gates

- **Run locally, exit 0:**
  - `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`
  - `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new citations)
  - `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `check-test-path-roots`
  - `check-doc-links`
  - the governed-surface test: NOT GOVERNED.
- **eslint on the changed files:** 0 errors. The warning counts on the pre-existing files are the same at base and head (3 and 7), and the new test has 0.
- **NOT MEASURED locally: `check-readme-exports`.** Its prerequisite is missing: 8 packages are unbuilt, so their `dist/index.d.ts` is not on disk. This edit adds no fenced block or import. CI's repo gates build `./packages/*` before running it.
- **Left to CI:** the full lint, the test shards and the performance budget.

## Acceptance notes

- **`PageView`'s Edit-in-studio (the dispatch asked).** I recommend it follow the Design entry. Not changed here.
  - On a page route the console offers three Studio-labelled handles. The app bar's pencil and the app switcher's Studio row go to `/studio/PACKAGE/interfaces?surface=page:NAME`; `AppHeader.pageRouteNoAuthoringHandles-12198` pins both. `PageView`'s `openInStudio` goes to `/apps/APP/metadata/page/NAME`.
  - With this PR, the sidebar's Design for that page also goes to Studio. That leaves `PageView`'s pencil, labelled "Edit in studio", as the only handle on the page route with another destination: the same one-designer-two-destinations shape this card removes.
  - Routing it through `appStudioRoutePath` would also hide it for a page whose app has no owning package. Today that pencil is the editor there, so this needs the same A3 ruling.
  - This is a source reading, not a browser measurement. Carrier: the dispatching domain:ui seat.
- **Ruled consequence of A3.** Entries of apps with no owning package Studio can open (runtime apps, `sys_metadata`) lose the Design entry they have had since the sidebar menu landed. It used to open the metadata-admin page, which can edit DB-authored items. The app bar never offered a pencil there.
- **Edge, not measured in any real app.** An object named `dashboard`, `page`, `report` or `system` gets the package's plain Data tab, as the app bar does. Its list route collides with those console routes anyway.
